title: 采桑子（轻舟短棹西湖好）
titleEn: Picking Mulberries (West Lake in a Little Boat)
author: 欧阳修
intro: An old statesman, newly retired, drifts across a lake in a small boat. The water is so still the boat seems not to move — until a bird takes off from the shore.
analysis: 欧阳修晚年退休，住在颍州（今安徽阜阳），写了十首《采桑子》，每首都以“西湖好”开头。这里的西湖是颍州西湖，不是杭州西湖。这一首写坐小船游湖：绿水弯弯曲曲，长堤上长满芳草，远远传来的音乐好像一路跟着船走。下阕写得特别细：没有风，水面像琉璃（玻璃一样的宝石）一样光滑，人坐在船上感觉不到船在动；只有水面轻轻荡开的波纹，和被惊起、擦着岸边飞走的水鸟，才告诉你船其实在走。这是“以动写静”——用一点点动静衬出湖面的安静。全词没有一个字写心情，但能读出一个老人放下官场后的轻松自在。
analysisEn: In retirement Ouyang Xiu settled in Yingzhou (today’s Fuyang in Anhui) and wrote a set of ten lyrics to the tune “Picking Mulberries”, each beginning “West Lake is lovely”. This is Yingzhou’s West Lake, not the more famous one in Hangzhou. Here he goes out in a light boat with a short oar. Green water winds ahead, fragrant grass covers the long dyke, and faint music from other pleasure boats seems to follow him everywhere. The second half is beautifully observed. There is no wind, and the surface is as smooth as glass — so smooth he can’t feel the boat moving at all. Only two things give the movement away: the tiny ripples spreading from the hull, and a shore bird that startles and skims off along the bank. Using a small movement to show how still everything is (“using motion to depict stillness”) is a favourite technique of Chinese poets. The poem never mentions his feelings, but you can sense the ease of a man who has finally put down the burdens of office.
background: Ouyang Xiu (1007–1072) was a leading statesman, historian and essayist of the Northern Song. He loved Yingzhou’s West Lake from his time as its prefect and retired there in 1071, the year before he died; this set of lyrics comes from those last years.
pronunciation: 棹 zhào（船桨）。逶迤 wēi yí（“迤”在这里读 yí）。“处处”读 chù chù。“掠”读 lüè。涟漪 lián yī。
version: 采用通行文本（《六一词》，《采桑子》十首之一，初中语文课外古诗词选文）。

lines.py: qīng zhōu duǎn zhào xī hú hǎo
lines.lit: Light boat, short oar — West Lake is lovely;
lines.en: In a light boat with a short oar, West Lake is lovely:

lines.py: lǜ shuǐ wēi yí, fāng cǎo cháng dī
lines.lit: green water winding, fragrant grass on the long dyke,
lines.en: green water winding away, sweet grass along the long dyke,

lines.py: yǐn yǐn shēng gē chù chù suí
lines.lit: faint pipes and songs follow everywhere.
lines.en: and faint music drifting after me wherever I go.

lines.py: wú fēng shuǐ miàn liú lí huá
lines.lit: No wind — the water’s surface is smooth as glass;
lines.en: Not a breath of wind; the lake is smooth as glass,

lines.py: bù jué chuán yí, wēi dòng lián yī
lines.lit: I do not feel the boat moving; slightly stirring ripples —
lines.en: I can’t feel the boat moving — only small ripples spreading,

lines.py: jīng qǐ shā qín lüè àn fēi
lines.lit: startled, a sand bird rises and skims the bank in flight.
lines.en: and a startled shore bird lifting off, skimming low along the bank.

words.note: 这里指颍州西湖，在今安徽阜阳。
书面语仍用，如“山路逶迤”。
现代汉语仍用，如“隐隐约约”。
笙是一种吹奏乐器，笙歌泛指奏乐唱歌。
古代指一种光滑透亮的宝石或烧制材料，现代有“琉璃瓦”。
现代汉语仍用，如“不知不觉”。
禽：鸟。今天“家禽”“飞禽”还用。

imagery.name: 西湖
imagery.zh: 颍州西湖安静、清澈，是作者退休后放松身心的地方。
imagery.en: The calm, clear West Lake of Yingzhou is where the retired statesman finally relaxes.

imagery.name: 船
imagery.zh: 轻舟慢慢漂，船动得感觉不到，写出湖面的平静和人的悠闲。
imagery.en: The little boat moves so gently it seems still — a picture of the calm lake and the calm man in it.

imagery.name: 笙
imagery.zh: 远处隐隐的笙歌给安静的湖面添了一点人间的热闹。
imagery.en: Faint music from far off adds a touch of human cheer to the quiet lake.

imagery.name: 鸟
imagery.zh: 被惊飞的水鸟是全词唯一的“大动作”，反衬湖面的静。
imagery.en: The startled bird is the only sudden movement in the poem, and it makes the stillness around it stand out.
